problems.field: participants.n_analyzed and participants.exclusions ('The favorite counts imply 49 per arm'); also eligibility.reason, open_questions[1], and reconciliation.agreed_fields_checked['studies[S1].participants.n_analyzed and eligibility.criterion_2_at_least_50_people'] (confirmed: true)
problems.form_value: n_analyzed = 98 ('124 minus 26', matched to 63 male + 35 female and to 882 favorites = 98 x 9). Exclusions: 'The favorite counts imply 49 per arm (all 441 human-AI favorites = 49 x 9), but the paper does not give the split.' The form notes no conflict between this split and the printed tests.
problems.source_says: The paper prints no analyzed count and no arm sizes. Its per-participant Mann-Whitney tests cannot come from 98 people split 49/49. Under 49 x 49 (mean U 1200.5, SD 140.7), the printed W values give p = 0.024 for the average number of ideas (printed p < 0.001), p = 0.0016 for the Effort item (printed 0.027), and p = 0.44 for the item on creating many ideas (printed 0.043). Ties can only raise |z|, so they cannot close these gaps. If the absolute-count test uses all three images per person (147 rows per arm), it gives p = 0.011 (printed p < 0.001). The printed values fit about 91 to 92 people in near-equal arms, or arms of roughly 30 and 70 people. So either fewer than 98 people entered the tests, or the arms were unequal and the 441 + 441 favorite split is wrong. The form treats 98 analyzed and 49 per arm as consistent and marks 98 confirmed. Criterion 2 is not at risk: the Raw TLX Welch df of 88.811 needs at least 91 people (df <= n1 + n2 - 2), and W = 1519.5 <= n1 x n2 needs at least 78.
problems.quote: This test indicated significant differences for the absolute count (W = 12652, p < 0.001) and the average number of ideas (1519.5, p < 0.001).

confirmed.statement: S1 recruited 124 people on Prolific and excluded 26 who did not complete the task, so 98 completed. The sex split (63 male + 35 female) also sums to 98. The paper never prints 98 for this phase, as the form says.
confirmed.quote: For this first part of the study, we recruited 124 participants using the online platform Prolific. 26 participants were excluded due to not completing the task.

confirmed.statement: At the meme-creation stage the favorite counts fit 98 people and 49 per arm: 882 favorites = 98 x 9, and 'all 441' collaborative favorites = 49 x 9, which leaves 441 baseline favorites, of which 415 were usable.
confirmed.quote: Due to technical problems, only 415 for the baseline conditions and all 441 for the collaborative condition were usable.

confirmed.statement: The people counts are people. Memes (415 and 441 usable favorites, 335 and 307 after curation, 150 per arm rated, 150 AI-only) appear only as n_units of the rating outcomes (300 for S1, 450 for S2). The 98 raters (100 recruited) are not counted as participants. S1-O4 leaves n_units null.
confirmed.quote: we then randomly sampled 10 images for each combination of background picture and topic, which, at five remaining images and three topics, left us with 150 images from the baseline and 150 images from the collaborative condition.

confirmed.statement: No count at assignment and no arm size is printed in the text, Figures 4 to 8, or Table 1, and the PDF has no appendix. n_randomized = null and the null arm counts are right.
The abstract's 'three groups of 50 participants each' includes the AI-only group, which had no people, so it conflicts with Section 3.6. The form flags this conflict.

confirmed.statement: S2 has no people of its own. Its human arms are 150 + 150 memes sampled from the S1 memes, and its AI arm is 150 GPT-4o memes. The same 98 raters scored all three. The form keeps S2's people counts null with counts_are 'other' and records the reuse of S1 creators in S2's arms and 'who'.
confirmed.quote: Along with the memes from the two conditions before, we had an additional condition with memes created exclusively using AI with no human input.
confirmed.locator: p. 7, Section 4.2; p. 5, Section 3.2; p. 6, Section 3.6

confirmed.statement: No other paper is said to use these participants. candidates.json has no other record by these authors or of this study (the other humor records, c230 and c333, have different authors). The seed meta-analysis list cites the paper once (Holzner et al., HAI16), as a synthesis. The blank sample_overlap matches 117 of the 124 final forms.

Criterion 2 holds for S1 by itself under any reading: 98 completed, at least 91 entered the Raw TLX test, and at least 78 entered the per-participant idea test, which is scored on the output. This verdict covers the count only. The paper still does not say how people were allocated to conditions (criterion 1).
confirmed.quote: we conducted statistical hypothesis tests on the number of ideas per participant.

summary: S1 clears 50 people by itself under any reading: 98 of 124 Prolific recruits completed (p. 6, Section 3.6), and the printed tests need at least 91 people for the Raw TLX t-test and at least 78 for the per-participant idea test, so criterion 2 holds, though allocation to conditions (criterion 1) is still not stated. The coding is refuted on one detail: the form treats 98 analyzed and an implied 49 per arm as confirmed, but the printed Mann-Whitney statistics cannot come from 49 + 49 people (they imply fewer than 98 analyzed or unequal arms), and the form does not flag this.
